title: Copy between two resources declared in one try

blocks.text: One try-with-resources statement can manage several resources. They are declared in the order they depend on each other and closed in the reverse order, and each one that was opened is closed.
Write `Transfer.copy(Opener opener)`. It opens a channel named `"in"`, then a channel named `"out"`, writes to `out` what `in.read()` returns, and closes both.
With channels that record what happens to them, a successful copy of `"data"` gives:
open in, open out, read in, write out data, close out, close in
Every `IOException` reaches the caller. Consider what must happen to `"in"` when `"out"` cannot be opened at all.

cases.says: It copies what "in" reads to "out" and closes both.
Resources close in reverse order of declaration: "out" before "in".
When opening "out" fails, the "in" already opened is still closed and the failure reaches the caller.

concepts: Resources are declared in the order they depend on each other, and when a later one fails to open, the ones already opened are still closed.
Several resources can share one statement, and they are closed in the reverse order of their declaration.
